faqs.question: Who should take this Full Stack Web Development course?
faqs.answer: This is for complete beginners who've never written a line of code, as well as anyone with some HTML/CSS experience who wants to go all the way to building real, deployed full-stack applications with React, Next.js, and MERN.

faqs.question: Can I pay for just one step instead of the whole course?
faqs.answer: Yes! You can start with just one step for as little as ₦30,000. Each step has its own price, and you can add more whenever you're ready. If you're able to take the full course at once, it works out cheaper (₦395,000 instead of ₦430,000 if bought step by step) — but starting small is always an option.

faqs.question: Do I need any prior coding experience?
faqs.answer: No. We start from Step 1 with HTML and CSS, assuming zero coding background. If you already know HTML/CSS or JavaScript, you're welcome to start further along the path.

faqs.question: Can I pick any step, or do I have to go in order?
faqs.answer: We strongly recommend going in order, since almost every later step directly builds on the JavaScript and React skills from earlier ones. You're still free to start wherever you like — if you skip ahead, we'll let you know clearly what you might want to brush up on first.

faqs.question: What's the difference between a Step Certificate and the Full Course Certificate?
faqs.answer: Every step you complete earns its own Digitanotion Step Certificate. Once you've completed all 8 steps, you also receive the Digitanotion Full Stack Web Developer Certificate, recognised by our industry partners as full-stack, MERN-ready developer readiness.

faqs.question: What if I only finish a few steps? Do I lose anything?
faqs.answer: Not at all. You keep every Step Certificate you've earned, and you can come back and continue at any time — there's no deadline or expiry on picking up where you left off.

faqs.question: What is the MERN stack, and why do you teach it?
faqs.answer: MERN stands for MongoDB, Express, React, and Node.js — four technologies that work together to build a complete web application, frontend to backend. It's one of the most in-demand skill combinations for web developer roles today, in Nigeria and globally.

faqs.question: What tools and software do I need?
faqs.answer: A laptop with at least 8GB RAM and a stable internet connection. All the software you need — a code editor, Node.js, MongoDB — is free, and we walk you through installing everything during orientation.

faqs.question: Will I build real projects I can show employers?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every step includes a hands-on lab, and the final step is a full capstone project — a complete, deployed MERN application connecting everything you've learned, ready to add to your portfolio.

faqs.question: What career opportunities does this lead to?
faqs.answer: Graduates are ready for roles like Junior Frontend Developer, Junior Full Stack Developer, React Developer, or Junior Backend Developer — and many go on to freelance or join Digitanotion's own project teams.

faqs.question: How much time should I set aside each week?
faqs.answer: About 8–12 hours a week works well: a few hours for live sessions, a few for hands-on labs, and some time for practice on your own. It's designed to fit around work, school, or family life.

faqs.question: Are the labs real projects, or just exercises?
faqs.answer: Both — early labs are focused exercises to build specific skills, while later labs (and the final capstone) are real, complete projects: a working REST API, a deployed Next.js site, and a full MERN application.

faqs.question: What support do I get during the course?
faqs.answer: A dedicated mentor, round-the-clock access to your practice labs, a student community, weekly office hours, and career guidance once you're done.

faqs.question: Is this course only for people who want to become developers?
faqs.answer: Not at all. Business owners who want to build their own websites, designers who want to code their own work, and career changers exploring tech are all welcome — the step-by-step format means you can stop wherever your goal is met.
